source.snippet: I had the misfortune of China Eastern Airlines losing my luggage. It's been several months now, with no more hope of finding it. My fiancée's jewellery box was inside, and I can provide at least €2,000 of invoices for the contents. However, China Eastern is only offering €300 in compensation. And AirAdvisor didn't help at all — not one bit. It was a flight from Japan to Paris with a connection in Shanghai. What can I do to ramp up the pressure? Or are there basically no laws protecting me because...

problem_statement: Airline passengers with documented losses far exceeding airline compensation caps (e.g. €7,000 loss, €300 offer) have no effective low-cost advocacy service to escalate claims — existing services like AirAdvisor are failing to deliver results, leaving passengers with no recourse.
target_segment: International air travelers who have suffered significant lost or damaged baggage losses and received inadequate airline compensation offers
notes: Poster had €7,000 in documented losses and only received €300. Explicitly states that a paid third-party service (AirAdvisor) failed them. Willingness to pay for effective advocacy is implied by the gap between loss and compensation. Opportunity: contingency-fee or flat-fee escalation service (legal letters, consumer authority filings, credit card chargeback guidance) targeting EU/Montreal Convention routes where liability limits are navigable. Recurring demand given frequency of airline baggage incidents globally. Single data point here but known pattern across travel forums.
